components: Saga pattern: starts a business workflow
Saga pattern: commits one local step
Saga pattern: commits the next local step
links: report control data to Workflow coordinator

steps: The saga durably records and executes local step A.
It advances to committed step B without a global transaction.
Step C fails after earlier effects are visible.
The saga resumes compensating actions in reverse semantic order until resolved.

lesson.scenario: A concert package reserves a ticket, books a train, then compensates both when the hotel sells out.

steps.title: Open the package saga
steps.narration: PKG-8 starts with a durable pointer to the first local transaction.
steps.outcome: Recovery can resume PKG-8 without a global database transaction.
steps.invariant: Progress is durable before a command may be retried.

steps.title: Reserve the concert ticket
steps.narration: The box office commits its own transaction; the reservation is now externally visible.
steps.outcome: Ticket success does not imply package success.
steps.invariant: Every committed forward step has a defined semantic compensation.

steps.title: Book the train
steps.narration: The rail reservation service commits seat C7 and the saga advances to the hotel.
steps.outcome: Two independent local commits exist at once.
steps.invariant: Forward steps execute in saga order and are idempotent.

steps.title: Detect the sold-out hotel
steps.narration: Room H-3 is sold before the command arrives, so PKG-8 records failure and switches direction.
steps.outcome: The saga cannot roll back databases; it must issue business cancellations.
steps.invariant: A failed later step never erases earlier committed facts.

steps.title: Compensate in reverse order
steps.narration: The train is canceled first and the ticket is then released, with each result recorded.
steps.outcome: PKG-8 ends consistently, although its intermediate reservations were visible.
steps.invariant: Compensations are durable, idempotent, and applied in reverse dependency order.
